lines.text: Seven gates stand between you and the scale. Each has three who mind it. One calls, one watches, one keeps.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The First Gate.

lines.text: You have read it. Now it is read over you.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The First Gate.

lines.text: Take this. It is empty. Every soul who walks the Duat writes its own road.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The First Gate.

lines.text: So is every road, before it is walked.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The First Gate.

lines.text: That one is Sad of Voice. He announces everyone the same way. Do not take it to heart.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The First Gate.

lines.text: Speak a name in the Duat and its owner must answer. Try his.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The First Gate.

lines.text: He hears everything. That is his work.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The First Gate.

lines.text: It does not need one written. Face-downward, Numerous of Shapes. You have met.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The First Gate.

lines.text: A gate is not opened by force. It is opened by being known.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The First Gate.

lines.text: I can give you the first gate. I cannot give you the others.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The First Gate.

lines.text: They forgot.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The Field That Waits.

lines.text: Here the dead are given fields. This one is yours. It is waiting.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The Field That Waits.

lines.text: In the old tongue the word is wen. In yours, open. Say it to what is shut.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The Field That Waits.

lines.text: Then something must carry it. Your worker sleeps on its feet. Res. Wake.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The Field That Waits.

lines.text: It does exactly what it is told. Nothing more.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The Field That Waits.

lines.text: Every pour breaks the water. Look at the worker. It will never stop unless it is told.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The Field That Waits.

lines.text: Hetep. Peace. The word is still.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The Field That Waits.

lines.text: Not the water. What keeps breaking it?
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The Field That Waits.

lines.text: That word is not yours yet. The land will give it to you when you need it.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The Field That Waits.

lines.text: The worker stopped, and you remembered. That is the whole of Wernes.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The Field That Waits.

lines.text: Your field is still waiting.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The Field That Waits.

lines.text: Here you are not required to labour.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The House With One Door.

lines.text: That is the question the land is asking.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The House With One Door.

lines.text: Nothing you know stops water. There is a word for it. You have been afraid of it a long time.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The House With One Door.

lines.text: You know it exists. Your mouth will not make it. Ask the door on the wall why.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The House With One Door.

lines.text: A shut door kept the night out of that house for years. Use the word for something small.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The House With One Door.

lines.text: A seal is not only a wall. Sometimes it is a hand over a cup.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: The House With One Door.

lines.text: Walk the row. Each worker hears whoever stands beside it.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: Shabti Row.

lines.text: Then give the water somewhere to go. Your workers carry.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: Shabti Row.

lines.text: They all answer to that word. Stand beside the one you mean.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: Shabti Row.

lines.text: Look closer at what you are speaking to.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: Shabti Row.

lines.text: They put it in your tomb. It answers for you when the fields call.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: Shabti Row.

lines.text: Nobody told it to.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: Shabti Row.

lines.text: It stopped. And the canal sank with it. Everything in this row was fed by its labour.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: Shabti Row.

lines.text: And tonight you said it to stop. Remember how. You will need it.
lines.context: The god Anpu (Anubis) guiding the dead priest Ankhu through the Duat. Warm, grave, kind, unhurried. Never theatrical. Scene: Shabti Row.
